definition: to mention a topic so people can discuss it
example: Can you bring up the budget issue in tomorrow's meeting?
exampleEs: ¿Puedes sacar el tema del presupuesto en la reunión de mañana?
cloze: Can you ____ the budget issue in tomorrow's meeting?
note: Also means 'to raise a child'. Not the same as 'grow up'.

definition: to think of an idea, plan or solution
example: Our team came up with a simple fix for the login bug.
exampleEs: Nuestro equipo ideó una solución sencilla para el error de inicio de sesión.
cloze: Our team ____ a simple fix for the login bug.
note: Three words, always together: come up with.

definition: to do or complete a task, test or plan
example: We carried out a small survey among our users last week.
exampleEs: Realizamos una pequeña encuesta entre nuestros usuarios la semana pasada.
cloze: We ____ a small survey among our users last week.
note: Formal and common in reports. It is not 'carry on' (continuar).

definition: to understand something or find the answer after thinking
example: I still can't figure out why the build keeps failing.
exampleEs: Todavía no logro averiguar por qué la compilación sigue fallando.
cloze: I still can't ____ why the build keeps failing.
note: Informal and very common. Similar to 'work out'.

definition: to tell people something they may not have noticed
example: She pointed out a mistake in the final report.
exampleEs: Ella señaló un error en el informe final.
cloze: She ____ a mistake in the final report.
note: Often followed by 'that': 'He pointed out that we were late'.

definition: to meet someone or find a problem by chance
example: I ran into a former colleague at the airport yesterday.
exampleEs: Me topé con un excolega en el aeropuerto ayer.
cloze: I ____ a former colleague at the airport yesterday.
note: Spanish speakers sometimes say 'encounter'; 'run into' is more natural in speech.

definition: to arrange, create or prepare something
example: Could you set up a call with the design team for Friday?
exampleEs: ¿Podrías organizar una llamada con el equipo de diseño para el viernes?
cloze: Could you ____ a call with the design team for Friday?
note: As a noun it is 'setup' (one word): 'a simple setup'.

definition: to delay something until a later time
example: We put off the release because of a critical security bug.
exampleEs: Pospusimos el lanzamiento por un error de seguridad crítico.
cloze: We ____ the release because of a critical security bug.
note: Followed by -ing, not an infinitive: 'put off starting', not 'put off to start'.

definition: to investigate or study a problem
example: The security team is looking into the strange login attempts.
exampleEs: El equipo de seguridad está investigando los intentos de inicio de sesión extraños.
cloze: The security team is ____ the strange login attempts.
note: It takes an object and the object goes after 'into': 'look into it'.

definition: to make your message clear to other people
example: It was hard to get across how complex the system really is.
exampleEs: Fue difícil hacer entender lo complejo que realmente es el sistema.
cloze: It was hard to ____ how complex the system really is.
note: Very common in the phrase 'get your point across'.

definition: to support a claim with proof, or to make a copy of data
example: Please back up your files before you update the system.
exampleEs: Por favor, haz una copia de seguridad de tus archivos antes de actualizar el sistema.
cloze: Please ____ your files before you update the system.
note: The noun is 'backup' (one word): 'a daily backup'.

definition: to complete something you said you would do
example: He always follows through on his promises to clients.
exampleEs: Él siempre cumple las promesas que les hace a los clientes.
cloze: He always ____ on his promises to clients.
note: Usually 'follow through on' + thing. The noun 'follow-through' means completing an action.

definition: to finally be in a place or situation, often without planning it
example: We ended up using a simpler design than we planned.
exampleEs: Terminamos usando un diseño más simple del que habíamos planeado.
cloze: We ____ using a simpler design than we planned.
note: Use -ing after it: 'end up working', not 'end up to work'.

definition: to refuse an offer or request, or to lower a volume or setting
example: She turned down the job offer because the salary was too low.
exampleEs: Ella rechazó la oferta de trabajo porque el salario era muy bajo.
cloze: She ____ the job offer because the salary was too low.
note: Opposite of 'accept'. For volume, the opposite is 'turn up'.

definition: to decide that something is not possible or not suitable
example: The doctors ruled out a serious infection after the tests.
exampleEs: Los médicos descartaron una infección grave después de los análisis.
cloze: The doctors ____ a serious infection after the tests.
note: Often used in the negative: 'We can't rule out a delay'.

definition: to learn a fact or discover information
example: I found out about the schedule change this morning.
exampleEs: Me enteré del cambio de horario esta mañana.
cloze: I ____ about the schedule change this morning.
note: 'Find out' is to discover; 'know' is to already have the information.

definition: to solve a problem or organize something that is confusing
example: Let's sort out the details before we talk to the client.
exampleEs: Resolvamos los detalles antes de hablar con el cliente.
cloze: Let's ____ the details before we talk to the client.
note: Informal; common in British English, also used in the US.

definition: to find a solution or calculate something; to exercise
example: We need to work out how much the project will cost.
exampleEs: Necesitamos calcular cuánto costará el proyecto.
cloze: We need to ____ how much the project will cost.
note: Has two meanings: solve/calculate and exercise at the gym. Context tells you which.

definition: to check or review something carefully
example: Let's go over the main points one more time.
exampleEs: Repasemos los puntos principales una vez más.
cloze: Let's ____ the main points one more time.
note: Very common in meetings: 'Can we go over the agenda?'

definition: to do something more about a topic or message you already started
example: I'll follow up with you by email after the call.
exampleEs: Te daré seguimiento por correo después de la llamada.
cloze: I'll ____ with you by email after the call.
collocations: follow up on an action item
note: As a noun or adjective it is 'follow-up': 'a follow-up email'.

definition: to learn the latest news or reach the same level as others
example: Let's have coffee and catch up on everything.
exampleEs: Tomemos un café y pongámonos al día con todo.
cloze: Let's have coffee and ____ on everything.
note: 'Catch up with' a person, 'catch up on' a topic or task.

definition: to register at a hotel or airport, or to ask how someone or something is doing
example: I'm just checking in to see how the migration is going.
exampleEs: Solo quería ver cómo va la migración.
cloze: I'm just ____ to see how the migration is going.
note: At work, 'check in with' means a short update or conversation.

definition: to wait before doing something
example: We should hold off on announcing the news until Monday.
exampleEs: Deberíamos esperar para anunciar la noticia hasta el lunes.
cloze: We should ____ on announcing the news until Monday.
note: Often with 'on': 'hold off on the update'.

definition: to succeed in doing something difficult
example: I can't believe the team pulled off the launch in two weeks.
exampleEs: No puedo creer que el equipo lograra el lanzamiento en dos semanas.
cloze: I can't believe the team ____ the launch in two weeks.
note: Informal. The meaning is positive: it was hard, and they did it.

definition: to accept a task, responsibility or challenge
example: I'm happy to take on the new project.
exampleEs: Con gusto me encargo del nuevo proyecto.
cloze: I'm happy to ____ the new project.
note: Also means 'to hire': 'The company took on ten new developers'.

definition: to leave an important position or job
example: The CEO will step down at the end of the year.
exampleEs: El director general dejará su cargo a fin de año.
cloze: The CEO will ____ at the end of the year.
note: The opposite is 'step in' (to help in a situation) or 'take over'.

definition: to finish something, especially a meeting or a project
example: Let's wrap up the meeting; we're running out of time.
exampleEs: Terminemos la reunión; se nos está acabando el tiempo.
cloze: Let's ____ the meeting; we're running out of time.
note: Common at the end of meetings: 'To wrap up, ...'.

definition: to introduce a new product or feature step by step
example: They plan to roll out the new feature to all users next month.
exampleEs: Planean lanzar la nueva función a todos los usuarios el mes que viene.
cloze: They plan to ____ the new feature to all users next month.
note: The noun is 'rollout' (one word). Very common in tech and business.

definition: to divide something into smaller parts, or to stop working
example: Let's break down the problem into three smaller tasks.
exampleEs: Dividamos el problema en tres tareas más pequeñas.
cloze: Let's ____ the problem into three smaller tasks.
note: Also: 'The server broke down' (it stopped working) and 'break down in tears'.

definition: to cancel something that was planned
example: They called off the event because of the storm.
exampleEs: Cancelaron el evento por la tormenta.
cloze: They ____ the event because of the storm.
note: Not the same as 'call' (llamar). It means 'cancel'.

definition: to reduce the amount or size of something
example: We need to cut back on our cloud spending.
exampleEs: Necesitamos reducir nuestro gasto en la nube.
cloze: We need to ____ on our cloud spending.
note: Usually followed by 'on': 'cut back on'.

definition: to take action to solve a problem or handle a task
example: I'll deal with the customer complaints this afternoon.
exampleEs: Me ocuparé de las quejas de los clientes esta tarde.
cloze: I'll ____ the customer complaints this afternoon.
note: Not 'deal to' or 'deal in' for this meaning. Always 'deal with'.

definition: to leave something or someone at a place, or to decrease
example: I'll drop off the documents at your office this afternoon.
exampleEs: Dejaré los documentos en tu oficina esta tarde.
cloze: I'll ____ the documents at your office this afternoon.
note: Also 'to fall asleep' (informal) and 'to decrease': 'Traffic dropped off'.

definition: to complete a form, or to replace someone temporarily
example: Please fill in the form and send it back to HR.
exampleEs: Por favor, rellena el formulario y envíaselo a Recursos Humanos.
cloze: Please ____ the form and send it back to HR.
note: In US English 'fill out' a form is also common. 'Fill someone in' means to give them the latest information.

definition: to reply to someone after you have checked something
example: Let me check the numbers and get back to you tomorrow.
exampleEs: Déjame revisar los números y te respondo mañana.
cloze: Let me check the numbers and ____ you tomorrow.
note: Very useful in meetings when you do not know the answer yet.

definition: to stop trying or to stop a habit
example: Don't give up; you're very close to finding the bug.
exampleEs: No te rindas; estás muy cerca de encontrar el error.
cloze: Don't ____; you're very close to finding the bug.
note: Use -ing after it: 'give up smoking'.

definition: to start or continue doing something, often with permission
example: You can go ahead and send the invitation to the whole team.
exampleEs: Puedes proceder y enviar la invitación a todo el equipo.
cloze: You can ____ and send the invitation to the whole team.
note: By itself, 'Go ahead' means 'Please start'. The noun is 'the go-ahead' (approval).

definition: to give something or responsibility to someone else
example: She will hand over the project to Marco next week.
exampleEs: Ella le entregará el proyecto a Marco la próxima semana.
cloze: She will ____ the project to Marco next week.
note: The noun 'handover' is common in teams: 'a smooth handover'.

definition: to delay something, or to remain strong under pressure
example: A late approval is holding up the whole release.
exampleEs: Una aprobación tardía está retrasando todo el lanzamiento.
cloze: A late approval is ____ the whole release.
note: As a noun, 'a hold-up' means a delay. Also means to rob someone.

definition: to stay at the same level or speed as someone or something
example: It's hard to keep up with all the new AI tools.
exampleEs: Es difícil mantenerse al día con todas las nuevas herramientas de IA.
cloze: It's hard to ____ all the new AI tools.
note: Three words, followed by a thing or person. Use it for news, trends and speed.

definition: to feel happy about something that will happen soon
example: I'm looking forward to meeting the new team.
exampleEs: Tengo muchas ganas de conocer al nuevo equipo.
cloze: I'm ____ meeting the new team.
note: The 'to' here is a preposition, so use -ing: 'looking forward to hearing', not 'to hear'.

definition: to invent something, or to form a whole from parts
example: Don't make up an answer; just say you will check.
exampleEs: No inventes una respuesta; solo di que lo vas a revisar.
cloze: Don't ____ an answer; just say you will check.
note: 'Make up for' means to compensate. 'Be made up of' means to consist of.

definition: to lose a chance to enjoy or take part in something
example: If you skip the workshop, you'll miss out on a great chance to learn.
exampleEs: Si te saltas el taller, te perderás una gran oportunidad para aprender.
cloze: If you skip the workshop, you'll ____ on a great chance to learn.
note: Always 'miss out on' + thing. Not 'miss out of'.

definition: to choose not to take part in something
example: Users can opt out of data collection in the settings.
exampleEs: Los usuarios pueden optar por no participar en la recopilación de datos desde los ajustes.
cloze: Users can ____ of data collection in the settings.
note: The opposite is 'opt in'. Very common in privacy and software contexts.

definition: to collect something, to restart, or to learn something easily
example: I picked up some Python while I was working on that project.
exampleEs: Aprendí algo de Python mientras trabajaba en ese proyecto.
cloze: I ____ some Python while I was working on that project.
collocations: pick up where we left off
note: Many meanings: collect, answer (a call), restart, learn. Check the context.

definition: to make something seem less serious or important
example: The company tried to play down the problem with the data.
exampleEs: La empresa intentó restarle importancia al problema con los datos.
cloze: The company tried to ____ the problem with the data.
note: The opposite is 'play up' (to make something seem more important).

definition: to give information or a message to someone else
example: Could you pass on my thanks to the whole team?
exampleEs: ¿Podrías transmitirle mis agradecimientos a todo el equipo?
cloze: Could you ____ my thanks to the whole team?
note: Also 'to decline': 'I'll pass on that offer'.

definition: to suggest an idea, plan or person for discussion
example: She put forward a clever proposal to cut our costs.
exampleEs: Ella presentó una propuesta inteligente para reducir nuestros costos.
cloze: She ____ a clever proposal to cut our costs.
note: Formal. In meetings, you can also say 'I'd like to propose'.

definition: to contact someone, often to ask for help or start a conversation
example: Feel free to reach out if you have any questions.
exampleEs: No dudes en escribirme si tienes alguna pregunta.
cloze: Feel free to ____ if you have any questions.
note: Very common in business emails: 'I'm reaching out to...'. Usually followed by 'to'.

definition: to use all of something so that none is left
example: We ran out of time before we finished the demo.
exampleEs: Nos quedamos sin tiempo antes de terminar la demostración.
cloze: We ____ time before we finished the demo.
note: The subject is the person: 'We ran out of time'. Without 'of', 'run out' means the supply is gone: 'Time ran out'.

definition: to make something bigger or increase its capacity
example: We need to scale up our servers before the product launch.
exampleEs: Necesitamos escalar nuestros servidores antes del lanzamiento del producto.
cloze: We need to ____ our servers before the product launch.
note: The opposite is 'scale down'. Very common in startups and tech.

definition: to start a task with a clear goal, or to explain something clearly
example: We set out to build the simplest note-taking app.
exampleEs: Nos propusimos construir la aplicación de notas más simple.
cloze: We ____ to build the simplest note-taking app.
note: 'Set out to' + infinitive means 'to begin with a goal'. Different from 'set off' (start a trip).

definition: to arrive or appear at a place or event
example: Only five people showed up to the workshop.
exampleEs: Solo cinco personas se presentaron al taller.
cloze: Only five people ____ to the workshop.
note: Informal. 'Show off' is different: it means to boast.

definition: to register for a service, course or event
example: You can sign up for the webinar on our website.
exampleEs: Puedes registrarte en el seminario web en nuestro sitio.
cloze: You can ____ for the webinar on our website.
note: The noun is 'sign-up': 'a sign-up form'. Use 'for' after it.

definition: to become slower, or to make something slower
example: Can you slow down a little? I want to take notes.
exampleEs: ¿Puedes ir un poco más despacio? Quiero tomar notas.
cloze: Can you ____ a little? I want to take notes.
note: Useful phrase when someone speaks too fast in a meeting.

definition: to be easy to notice because of being better or different
example: Her presentation really stood out from the others.
exampleEs: Su presentación realmente destacó entre las demás.
cloze: Her presentation really ____ from the others.
note: Do not mix it up with 'stand for' (to represent).

definition: to start controlling or doing something that someone else did
example: Maria will take over the team when Alex leaves.
exampleEs: María asumirá la dirección del equipo cuando Alex se vaya.
cloze: Maria will ____ the team when Alex leaves.
note: A 'takeover' (noun) is when a company buys another.

definition: to start a new activity, or to use space or time
example: I took up running last year to manage my stress.
exampleEs: Empecé a correr el año pasado para manejar mi estrés.
cloze: I ____ running last year to manage my stress.
note: Also: 'take someone up on an offer' means to accept an offer.

definition: to join with another person or group to work together
example: We teamed up with a local startup to build the prototype.
exampleEs: Nos asociamos con una startup local para construir el prototipo.
cloze: We ____ with a local startup to build the prototype.
note: Always 'team up with' + person or company.

definition: to consider all the details and results of something carefully
example: Let's think through the risks before we choose a vendor.
exampleEs: Analicemos a fondo los riesgos antes de elegir un proveedor.
cloze: Let's ____ the risks before we choose a vendor.
note: Different from 'think over', which means to consider for some time.

definition: to have a particular result, especially a surprising one
example: The meeting turned out to be much shorter than expected.
exampleEs: La reunión resultó ser mucho más corta de lo esperado.
cloze: The meeting ____ to be much shorter than expected.
note: Often 'turn out to be' + noun or adjective: 'It turned out to be easy'.

definition: to test something to see if it works or if you like it
example: We tried out three different tools before choosing this one.
exampleEs: Probamos tres herramientas diferentes antes de elegir esta.
cloze: We ____ three different tools before choosing this one.
note: The noun is 'tryout'. 'Try on' is for clothes.

definition: to give your opinion in a discussion
example: Several engineers weighed in on the proposed change.
exampleEs: Varios ingenieros opinaron sobre el cambio propuesto.
cloze: Several engineers ____ on the proposed change.
note: Often 'weigh in on' + topic. Informal.

definition: to put information on paper or on a screen so you remember it
example: Please write down the main action items from the call.
exampleEs: Por favor, anota los puntos de acción principales de la llamada.
cloze: Please ____ the main action items from the call.
note: Different from 'write up', which means to produce a full written version.

definition: to stop using or providing something step by step
example: The company will phase out the old software by December.
exampleEs: La empresa retirará gradualmente el software antiguo para diciembre.
cloze: The company will ____ the old software by December.
note: The opposite is 'phase in' (to introduce gradually).

definition: to give the main points in a short form
example: To sum up, we need more time and a clearer scope.
exampleEs: En resumen, necesitamos más tiempo y un alcance más claro.
cloze: To ____, we need more time and a clearer scope.
note: A natural way to start your conclusion in a meeting: 'To sum up, ...'.

definition: to fail to happen, especially a plan or deal
example: The deal fell through at the last minute.
exampleEs: El trato se cayó a último minuto.
cloze: The deal ____ at the last minute.
collocations: fall through at the last minute
note: Used for plans and agreements, not for people.

definition: to be as good as people expected
example: The product didn't live up to the hype.
exampleEs: El producto no estuvo a la altura de la expectativa.
cloze: The product didn't ____ the hype.
note: Three words. Usually with 'expectations', 'hype' or 'reputation'.

definition: to find something by chance, or to seem a certain way
example: I came across a great article about vector databases.
exampleEs: Me topé con un excelente artículo sobre bases de datos vectoriales.
cloze: I ____ a great article about vector databases.
note: 'Come across as' + adjective describes the impression you give: 'You come across as confident'.

definition: to use something as a base for further progress
example: We can build on the results from the first pilot.
exampleEs: Podemos construir sobre los resultados del primer piloto.
cloze: We can ____ the results from the first pilot.
note: Different from 'build up', which means to increase gradually.
